accepted.question_text: Let N be a sufficiently large prime, and let H_2^+(N) denote the set of weight-2 newforms of level Γ_0(N) whose functional equation has sign +1. For each f in H_2^+(N), let L(f,s) be its L-function. Iwaniec and Sarnak proved that, as N tends to infinity, at least 50% of the central values L(f,1) are larger than (log N)^(-2). Is it true that more than 50% of these central values are nonzero?
accepted.context_brief: Central values of weight-2 newform L-functions

evidence.quote: Let N be a larger prime, and let H_2^+(N) be set of newforms of weight two for Γ_0(N) whose L-functions have even functional equation. We (Iwaniec-Sarnak) have recently proven that as N → ∞ at least 50% of the central values of L(f,s) for f in H_2^+(N) are larger than (log N)^-2.
Problem A. Show that more than 50% of these central values are nonzero.

accepted.question_text: In the same setting, with N a large prime and H_2^+(N) the weight-2 newforms of level Γ_0(N) with even functional equation, can one prove a stronger lower-bound statement: that more than 50% of the central values L(f,1) are at least (log N)^(-A) for some fixed positive constant A?

evidence.quote: Problem B. Better still, show that more than 50% of the central values are larger than (log N)^-A for some positive constant A.

accepted.question_text: Let (V,L) be a projective manifold over a number field k together with a metrized ample sheaf, so that one has a height function h_L: V(k) → R and an associated height zeta function Z(V,L;s)=Σ_{x∈V(k)} h_L(x)^(-s). For varieties V that are not toric, the source says that this zeta function does not seem to have satisfactory analytic properties, unlike classical Hasse-Weil-Serre L-functions. Can one find a class of generating series that counts the rational points V(k) in a mathematically useful way and has good analytic behavior?
accepted.context_brief: Generating series for rational points of arithmetic varieties

evidence.quote: Let (V,L) be a projective manifold over a number field k endowed with a metrized ample sheaf allowing one to construct the height function h_L : V(k) → R. The naive problem of finding asymptotics for the number of k-points of bounded height has the refined version: to understand the analytic properties of the height zeta-function Z(V,L;s) = Σ_{x∈V(k)} h_L(x)^-s.
Unfortunately, it seems that if V is not homogeneous or something like that, Z(V,L;s) does not have good analytic properties, unlike the more traditional Hasse-Weil-Serre ..., L-functions.
The problem I want to draw attention to is: Find a class of good generating series counting V(k).

accepted.question_text: Let K be a number field contained in C, and let S be a finite set of places of Q, possibly including archimedean places. Let G_{K,S} be the Galois group of the maximal algebraic subfield of C that is unramified outside S. Is there any example in which G_{Q,S} is abelian even though S contains at least one finite prime?
accepted.context_brief: Abelianity of Galois groups unramified outside S

evidence.quote: Let K be a number field contained in C and S a finite set of places of Q (possibly including archimedean places). Let G_{K,S} be the Galois group of the maximal algebraic subfield of C which is unramified outside of S.
Problem: Can one find instances where G_{Q,S} is abelian when S contains at least one finite prime?

accepted.question_text: Suppose X is a curve over a field of characteristic 0 and π: A → X is an abelian scheme over X. Let Γ be a group of sections of π, and assume that no element of Γ factors through a subfamily of group varieties of relative dimension 1. For a geometric point P in X(ḱ), let Γ_P denote the fiber of Γ above P. Must there be only finitely many points P for which rank(Γ_P)=rank(Γ)?

accepted.question_text: Fix a number field K and a positive integer g. Are there only finitely many rings that occur as endomorphism rings of g-dimensional abelian varieties defined over K?
accepted.context_brief: Finiteness of endomorphism rings over a number field

evidence.quote: Let K be a number field and g a positive integer. Then show that the number of distinct endomorphism rings of abelian varieties of dimension g defined over K is finite.

accepted.question_text: Let S be a finite set of rational primes, and let X(S) be the set of rational numbers x in Q such that both x and 1−x are S-units. The source asks for lower bounds on the size of X(S), or on the maximum of |X(S)| over all sets S with |S|=s. Does there exist a lower bound that grows faster than any polynomial in s?

evidence.quote: If S is a finite set of rational primes, let X(S) denote the set of rational numbers x ∈ Q such that both x and 1−x are S-units, and denote by N(s) the maximum of the cardinalities |X(S)| as S ranges through all finite sets of primes with |S| = s.
Problem: Is there a lower bound for |X(S)| (or for the maximum of the cardinalities |X(S)| ranging over sets S with |S| = s) which grows more than polynomially in s?
